rapport_notes: Excellent de-escalation of a frustrated, price-disputing customer — stayed calm, transparent, and non-defensive throughout, and made a real concession (reduced crew/hours).

evidence_quotes.agenda: "What specific concern you have on your estimate or on the estimate that we provided last Saturday?" — asked immediately at the top of this re-quote call, before further discovery.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Extensive real follow-up on the pricing disconnect: re-verified inventory, box count, crew size, and even asked about the customer's prior move to validate the adjustment, ultimately revising the quote from $2,700/4-person/7.5hr down to $1,152/2-person/6hr.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: Customer asked directly: "if it's not six hours, let's say they do it in three, are we still on the hook for six or do we only pay for those three?" Rep: "You will only be paying for three hours... we don't collect deposit because we charge on an hourly basis."

top_strength: Handled a heated price objection with total transparency — walked through the exact math, honestly reduced the crew/hours instead of defending the original number, and gave the clearest "pay only for actual hours" answer in the whole batch.
coaching_note: Never re-asks for the booking after settling on the revised price — call ends with the customer just requesting an emailed quote, missing a chance to close while trust was freshly rebuilt.
